title: CI/CD DORA Metrics (Real-time)

list.name: allowed_lateness_hours
list.label: Allowed lateness (hours)
list.description: Must match ALLOWED_LATENESS in DeploymentFrequencyOperator.java (currently Time.hours(1)) — update this value by hand if that constant ever changes. Not auto-synced.

list.name: deployment_frequency_window_seconds
list.label: Deployment frequency window size (seconds)
list.description: Must match FlinkConfig.DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_WINDOW (currently Time.days(1) = 86400s), which also sizes the live counter's bucket in LiveDeployCounter. Not auto-synced — update by hand if that constant changes.

panels.title: Current Watermark (job-global)
panels.description: The event-time watermark the whole job is currently at (WatermarkReporterOperator). To test truly-late handling: compare THIS value (not your test event's timestamp) against a window's window_alive_until in the panel below. Once this watermark passes that window's window_alive_until, an event timestamped inside that window (still [window_start, window_end) — window_alive_until never changes that range) will route to TRULY_LATE_TAG instead of updating the window.

targets.rawSql: SELECT value AS current_watermark FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'WATERMARK' AND pipeline_id = 'GLOBAL' ORDER BY inserted_at DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'LEAD_TIME_FOR_CHANGES' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (live)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'CHANGE_FAILURE_RATE_LIVE' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (window close)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'CHANGE_FAILURE_RATE' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'MEAN_TIME_TO_RECOVERY' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (live)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE_LIVE' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at
SELECT inserted_at AS "time", value, pipeline_id || ' (window close)' AS metric FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'PIPELINE_HEALTH_SCORE' AND $__timeFilter(inserted_at) ORDER BY inserted_at

panels.title: Live Metric Values
panels.description: window_start/window_end are computed, not stored — the live counter upserts one Postgres row per pipeline under a fixed 1970-01-01 sentinel (see LIVE_WINDOW_MARKER in DeploymentFrequencyOperator), so there's no real per-row window to select. These columns approximate the currently-open window by bucketing inserted_at into deployment_frequency_window_seconds-sized, epoch-aligned buckets — the same arithmetic LiveDeployCounter itself uses (ts / windowMs). Good enough to eyeball 'which window is live counting into right now', not a substitute for the Window History panel below.

targets.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (metric_type, pipeline_id) inserted_at AS "time", metric_type, pipeline_id, service_name, value, performance_band, to_timestamp(floor(extract(epoch FROM inserted_at) / $deployment_frequency_window_seconds) * $deployment_frequency_window_seconds) AS window_start, to_timestamp(floor(extract(epoch FROM inserted_at) / $deployment_frequency_window_seconds) * $deployment_frequency_window_seconds + $deployment_frequency_window_seconds) AS window_end FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_LIVE' ORDER BY metric_type, pipeline_id, inserted_at DESC

panels.title: Deployment Frequency — Window History
panels.description: window_alive_until = window_end + ALLOWED_LATENESS: how long (in watermark time, not event time) this window's state stays open for late corrections after it first fires. It does NOT extend which event_timestamps belong to this window — that's always [window_start, window_end), for on-time and late events alike. To test truly-late handling: push an event timestamped inside [window_start, window_end) only after the Current Watermark panel above already reads past this row's window_alive_until.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_timestamp(window_start_ms / 1000) AS window_start, to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS window_end, pipeline_id, service_name, value AS deploys_per_day, sample_count AS deploy_count, inserted_at AS computed_at, to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) + interval '$allowed_lateness_hours hours' AS window_alive_until FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY' ORDER BY window_end_ms DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Truly-Late Events — All Metrics (per event detail)
panels.description: Every event that missed its metric's allowed-lateness grace period, across all three windowed metrics that side-output truly-late data (DeploymentFrequencyOperator, DoraOperators.changeFailureRate, PipelineHealthOperator) — see TrulyLateAuditOperator. source_metric identifies which metric's window the event was too late for; it's the same underlying cicd_alerts LATE_EVENT audit trail regardless of event_type, so use source_metric (not event_type) to filter by metric.

targets.rawSql: SELECT inserted_at AS computed_at, payload->>'source_metric' AS source_metric, payload->>'event_id' AS event_id, payload->>'pipeline_id' AS pipeline_id, payload->>'service_name' AS service_name, payload->>'event_type' AS event_type, payload->>'event_time' AS event_time, payload->>'watermark_time' AS watermark_time FROM cicd_alerts WHERE alert_type = 'LATE_EVENT' ORDER BY inserted_at DESC LIMIT 20

_disabledPanels_readme: Panels below are not part of the active 'panels' array (Grafana ignores this key) — kept here so they're easy to restore. Move a panel object back into 'panels' to re-enable it.

_disabledPanels.title: Deployment Frequency — Truly-Late Events (count per window)
_disabledPanels._disabledReason: Backing metric (DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_LATE_EVENTS) is no longer sunk — LateEventOperator wiring commented out in PipelineObservabilityJob.java (see [C] there). Its processing-time 10-min window rarely closed before the job restarted, leaving this permanently on 'No data'. Live metrics, Window History, and the per-event detail panel above are unaffected.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_timestamp(window_start_ms / 1000) AS window_start, to_timestamp(window_end_ms / 1000) AS window_end, pipeline_id, service_name, value AS late_event_count, inserted_at AS computed_at FROM cicd_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'DEPLOYMENT_FREQUENCY_LATE_EVENTS' ORDER BY window_end_ms DESC LIMIT 20
